subject: Inference visibility rollout and staging access -- next steps
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@storify.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference observability for rollout

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Storify is moving the inference path for the recommendation service to a dedicated pool next month and our SREs want a short, concrete plan for how we’ll get visibility in staging before prod rollout. Specifically we want:
- Dashboard templates for P50/P95 latency, token rates, and per-model error rates
- Tracing hook placement and sampling guidance for the async batching layer
- Error taxonomy examples (model vs. infra vs. decode) and suggested alert thresholds
- A central runbook for on-call to use when the model degrades

Can you share a short rollout checklist and whether Redwood will need staging IAM/project access? Marco (cc’d) will coordinate the infra side.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of SRE, Storify AI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@storify.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-02T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Inference visibility for rollout

Elena — good questions and glad the demo was useful. Attached is a compact rollout checklist (redwood_visibility_rollout_checklist.xlsx) and a dashboard skeleton (dashboard_skeleton.png) you can preview. High level plan below and a proposed timeline:

1) Stage access & instrumentation (Days 0–3)
   - Storify adds a service account with Viewer + Logging/Tracing write to the staging project (we'll provide an IAM snippet)
   - Our impl team drops tracing hooks at the batching ingress and at the model decode boundary (we recommend 1% sampling for full traces initially)

2) Dashboard & alerts (Days 3–7)
   - Import dashboard skeleton, wire metrics: latency p50/p95, token throughput, batch size histogram, error split by category
   - Suggested alerts: p95 latency > 2.5x baseline sustained for 5m; model error rate > 3% over 10m; redis/Broker errors > 0.5%

3) Runbook & handoff (Days 7–10)
   - Publish short runbook with triage flow (check model variant, cache hit rate, backends). We’ll link to the playbook and Slack escalation policy.
   - Joint run-through with Storify on-call.

I’ve cc’d Neha and Laura to own the implementation tasks. Neha — can your team confirm the IAM snippet for Marco and whether we need a VPN/VPC peering step?

Attachments: redwood_visibility_rollout_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), dashboard_skeleton.png (preview)

Best,
Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Forwarding a short technical checklist — see inline.

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:22:00Z
Subject: Technical notes: staging access + tracing hooks
To: Elena Rossi <elena@storify.ai>, marco@storify.ai

Hi Elena / Marco,

Quick tech notes:
- IAM: please create a service account redwood-impl@storify-staging with roles/viewer, roles/logging.logWriter, roles/cloudtrace.agent and grant it to neha_kapoor@redwood.com and laura_bennett@redwood.com. If you prefer, we can accept a short-lived key via the secure upload link (see attached staging_access_instructions.pdf).
- Tracing placement: instrument the batching ingress (where requests are aggregated) and add a lightweight span at model.decode() boundary. Use Trace attributes: request_id, model_variant, batch_size, input_token_count.
- Sampling: start at 1% for full traces; bump to 5% around known experiments. For error traces we set explicit sampling flag to capture 100% of errors.
- Metrics: expose counters for total tokens, tokens_out, successful_infers, infer_errors{type}. Error taxonomy: 
   * MODEL_FAILURE — decode exceptions, softmax collapse, hallucination markers (post-eval)
   * INFRA_RETRY — connection/timeout/retry events to external stores
   * LATENCY_DEGRADATION — sustained queueing/backpressure

Please confirm once the service account is created and we’ll schedule the staging deploy.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: staging_access_instructions.pdf (instructions stub)

One ask: can Redwood add a brief section in the runbook that maps alert types to the error taxonomy you suggested? That will help our SRE rotation triage faster.

Elena
